checks.name: Program aim
checks.quote: The Master of Science program in Computer Science provides an opportunity for students to enhance their understanding of the principal hardware and software themes.

checks.name: Evening classes
checks.quote: Evening classes with a wide range of topics in computer science

checks.name: Department also plans an online M.S.
checks.quote: Online Master of Science in Computer Science

checks.name: Undergraduate CS presumption
checks.quote: The graduate program is based on the presumption that the student has an undergraduate degree with a major in computer science, or equivalent coursework in the principal computer science and mathematics subjects required

checks.name: Admission is competitive
checks.quote: These are minimum requirements for the program admission. Admission is competitive and meeting minimum requirement does not guarantee admission to the program.

checks.name: Unconditional GPA
checks.quote: Applicants seeking unconditional admission must have a bachelor's degree in Computer Science or closely related field with a GPA of 3.0 or better in all courses or the most recent 60 semester units attempted

checks.name: Unconditional topic coverage
checks.quote: 10-12 semester units including Calculus and Probability and Statistics

checks.name: Conditional admission
checks.quote: Applicants who do not meet unconditional admission but have a bachelor's degree with a GPA above 3.0 may seek conditional admission. However, priority will be given to unconditional admissions first.

checks.name: International students not conditionally admitted
checks.quote: However, per CSU Admissions and SEVIS Policy, international students attending the University on a visa requiring issuance of an I-20 will NOT be conditionally admitted and must meet all requirements prior to gaining admission to the University.

checks.name: Conditional students and aid
checks.quote: Students in conditional standing do not qualify for federal financial aid until they are in unconditional standing.

checks.name: English language requirement
checks.quote: must have passed the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) exam with a minimum score of 6.5 or the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) exam with a minimum score of 213 on the computer-based, or 550 on the paper-based, or 80 on the Internet-based TOEFL.

checks.name: Supplemental application form
checks.quote: This Program Application form is REQUIRED and applications missing this completed form uploaded to Cal State Mentor site may be declined without review.

checks.name: SOP, resume, letters, unofficial transcript
checks.quote: applicants are REQUIRED to submit a statement of purpose (why applying to CPP CS MS program and how it will help to achieve your career objectives), resume/CV, two letters of recommendation and unoffical pdf transcript on Cal State Apply.

checks.name: GRE not required
checks.quote: The department does not require the GRE. However, it is recommended that you take it if your major GPA does not meet the 3.0 requirement.

checks.name: GPA to maintain
checks.quote: A grade point average of 3.0 (B) or better must be maintained in all upper-division undergraduate and all graduate courses.

checks.name: Transfer unit cap
checks.quote: No more than 9 semester units of acceptable graduate credit may be transferred from another graduate institution.

checks.name: Combined transfer limit
checks.quote: A total limit of 9 semester units of transfer, Extended University, and/or units petitioned for graduate credit may be included on a master's contract. The stipulated time limit of 7 years applies to all of the above.

checks.name: Total units
checks.quote: TOTAL UNITS REQUIRED: 30 units

checks.name: 4000-level electives
checks.quote: Computer Science MS students can take up to 6 semester units of CS 4000+ levels elective classes to satisfy their elective courses requirement, excluding the following courses: CS 4000, CS 4310, CS 4610, CS 4620, CS 4630, and CS 4800.

checks.name: Required courses offered yearly
checks.quote: The required courses CS 5250, CS 5300, CS 5800 and CS 6640 are offered every year. All other graduate courses CS 5xxx are offered every two years.

checks.quote: Graduate courses traditionally meet in late afternoons and evenings.
